facet_lens: Meta-review — is the review process itself sound, are facets independent, is multispectrum-review v2.4.0 doctrine being followed, is evidence being incorporated correctly?
review_target: keystone bundle 2026-05-20 (14 foundational ADRs ADR-0242..ADR-0255 + 4 specs + 4 PRDs + 2 user-story compendia + 4 standards = 28 docs)
executive_summary: The keystone-bundle multispectrum review v2.4.0 has produced two high-quality input artefacts (audit-report + idea-refine deep-dive). The deep-dive's red-team posture is genuine, the audit is honest about defects (filename drift, missing onboarding docs, untagged placeholders) and the corpus is substantively production-grade. HOWEVER, from a META-REVIEW lens, the review PROCESS itself does NOT yet conform to multispectrum-review v2.4.0 doctrine in a critical way: the deep-dive document (which targets F1..F9 + M1+M2 + A1..A7) was authored as a SINGLE artefact by what appears to be a single author/agent context. Per the canonical consensus-debate-spectrum-lens-subagents directive (2026-05-14), each facet MUST be a SEPARATE subagent or teammate session — bias-collapse from one agent wearing multiple lenses is exactly the failure mode v2.2.0+ was created to prevent. The deep-dive is best classified as an INPUT to the multispectrum review (pre-debate evidence), not as the multispectrum review itself. The per-facet r1/r2 subagent dispatch wave still owes evidence, and only one r1 file (this M2 file) currently exists for the keystone change_id under evidence/debate/. CONDITIONAL-GO with required remediation before synthesis.

tier2_judgment_findings.title: Facet independence is not yet evidenced — single-author deep-dive is NOT a substitute for per-facet subagent debate
tier2_judgment_findings.doctrine_citation: feedback_consensus_debate_spectrum_lens_subagents — 'consensus debate should be done by separate subagents or separate teammate sessions ... with each spectrum as their lens'; feedback_multispectrum_review_v22 — 'Rule (executor_topology): Each facet → its OWN separate subagent or teammate session. NO reviewer_id appears across multiple facets within a single change_id. Lane refuses on violation.'
tier2_judgment_findings.evidence: The idea-refine deep-dive at docs/architecture/keystone-bundle-idea-refine-deep-dive.md declares review_facets_targeted as F1..F9 + M1+M2 + A1..A7 (15+ facets) inside a SINGLE document. The doctrine explicitly forbids one agent wearing multiple lenses. The deep-dive is high-quality, but it is structurally INPUT EVIDENCE to the multispectrum review, not the review itself. Treating it as the review would violate v2.4.0.
tier2_judgment_findings.remediation: Reclassify the deep-dive as 'pre-debate adversarial evidence package' (NOT as multispectrum review output). Dispatch the per-facet subagent wave (F1..F9 + M1 + A1..A7) — each subagent ingests the audit + deep-dive as INPUT and emits its own independent r1.json. The deep-dive's authored findings serve as a starting point but each facet subagent is free to disagree or extend.

tier2_judgment_findings.title: Facet coverage list is incomplete relative to v2.4.0 change-class triggers
tier2_judgment_findings.doctrine_citation: feedback_multispectrum_review_v22 — 'For CC-1 kernel public API + new microservice + new HTTP routes + new state machine: 12 facets (F1-F11 + M1+M2; F13 skipped if no breaking change)' + v2.1.0 additions F10 reversibility, F11 observability, F13 migration
tier2_judgment_findings.evidence: The deep-dive's review_facets_targeted frontmatter lists F1..F9 + M1+M2 + A1..A7. It is MISSING F10 reversibility (the bundle is a kernel-public-API-class change AND introduces multiple microservice boundaries AND modifies multiple state machines → F10 required), F11 observability (the bundle creates new HTTP routes via the network-topology ADR + adds the observability emission contract gap; F11 is structurally required), and F13 migration (the bundle supersedes ADR-0220 → ADR-0239 chain and supersedes/amends prior ADRs explicitly — a textbook breaking-change cluster).
tier2_judgment_findings.remediation: Add three more required facets to the dispatch wave: F10 reversibility (debugger subagent), F11 observability (tracer subagent), F13 migration (architect subagent). The keystone bundle qualifies for F10+F11+F13 by independent triggers.

tier2_judgment_findings.title: Change class for the bundle is not explicitly declared
tier2_judgment_findings.doctrine_citation: multispectrum-review change_classes (CC-1..CC-7) — 'CC-1 kernel_public_api → all facets deep + consensus_debate_required'
tier2_judgment_findings.evidence: Neither the audit nor the deep-dive declares the bundle's change_class. By inspection the bundle is unambiguously CC-1 (kernel public API: tenant-model, cedar-fragment-schema, compliance-pack-schema, platform-architecture all become canonical public contracts). CC-1 requires ALL facets deep + consensus_debate_required. Without an explicit declaration, downstream lane enforcement cannot verify the right facets were dispatched.
tier2_judgment_findings.remediation: Add explicit `change_class: CC-1 kernel_public_api` to the bundle's review manifest. Cite the trigger (new public spec contracts in /specs/platform-architecture.json + 14 keystone ADRs that supersede ADR-0220 and amend ADR-0145).

tier2_judgment_findings.title: Evidence synthesis quality is STRONG but synthesis itself has not been produced
tier2_judgment_findings.doctrine_citation: feedback_multispectrum_review_v22 — 'Synthesis required keys: consensus_points, consensus_shifts_from_round_1_to_round_2, unresolved_tensions, final_recommendation, termination_reason'
tier2_judgment_findings.evidence: The audit-report's §1.5 Top-five gaps + §7 GO/NO-GO recommendation + the deep-dive's red-team findings together contain the substantive material for a synthesis. They are NOT a synthesis in the v2.2.0+ structural sense (no consensus_points across distinct facet subagents, no consensus_shifts_from_round_1_to_round_2 because r2 hasn't happened, no per-facet reviewer_id attribution). Mechanical synthesis schema is unmet.
tier2_judgment_findings.remediation: After per-facet r1 + r2 emissions, produce evidence/debate/keystone-bundle-2026-05-20-synthesis.json with all required keys. The audit + deep-dive narratives can be cited as input artefacts in the synthesis, but cannot substitute for the structural required_keys.

tier2_judgment_findings.title: A-family adherence facets correctly invoked but their lane-trigger conditions not individually documented
tier2_judgment_findings.doctrine_citation: feedback_multispectrum_adherence_facets — 'Every change that touches a domain covered by an A-facet (any new file naming → A1; any new doc → A2; any new crate placement → A3; any kernel/adapter boundary change → A4; any new dep → A5; any new JSON schema → A6; any new algorithm/heuristic → A7) dispatches the corresponding adherence-facet subagent.'
tier2_judgment_findings.evidence: The deep-dive declares A1..A7 in scope. The triggers are clearly met (28 new docs → A2 + A1, 4 new JSON schemas → A6, multiple kernel/adapter boundary moves via ADR-0246 promotion → A4, multiple new dependencies in standards docs → A5, Cedar v4.2 + MLS RFC 9420 + HLC algorithm choices → A7). Triggers are met but the deep-dive does not show the lane-trigger justification per A-facet.
tier2_judgment_findings.remediation: When per-facet A1..A7 subagents emit r1.json, each must cite the specific trigger from the bundle that admits its dispatch (e.g., A6 cites /specs/tenant-model.json, A4 cites ADR-0246 §D-3, etc.).
tier2_judgment_findings.owner: each A-facet subagent in its r1.json

tier2_judgment_findings.title: Evidence-incorporation traceability is good in narrative form but lacks per-finding citation back to source artefacts
tier2_judgment_findings.doctrine_citation: multispectrum-review.json#consensus_debate_protocol.rounds.round_1_independent.required_keys — implicit traceability requirement (evidence must cite source)
tier2_judgment_findings.evidence: The deep-dive's F-MISSED-* and F-ANTI-* findings cite the audit report's gap framing well in §1 + §3 but individual findings (e.g., F-MISSED-9 logging format) don't carry a per-finding `evidence_pointer` field linking to the specific audit table row or deep-dive section the finding extends. This makes synthesis collation harder.
tier2_judgment_findings.remediation: Per-facet r1.json files should include an `evidence_pointers: [{source: 'audit-report#1.5', claim: '...'}]` array on each finding. This is a v2.4.0 best-practice add, not a hard requirement.
tier2_judgment_findings.owner: per-facet subagents in their r1 emissions

tier2_judgment_findings.title: Round-2 cross-subagent rebuttal mechanism is not yet scheduled
tier2_judgment_findings.doctrine_citation: feedback_multispectrum_review_v22 — 'Round 2 each subagent sees other subagents' Round-1 emissions; emits <change_id>-<facet-id>-r2.json with agreements / disagreements / shifted_position / new_evidence.'
tier2_judgment_findings.evidence: No dispatch plan or queue exists for r2. Without scheduled r2 emissions, the synthesis cannot populate `consensus_shifts_from_round_1_to_round_2`, which is a REQUIRED key in the synthesis schema.
tier2_judgment_findings.remediation: After r1 wave completes, dispatch r2 wave (each subagent reads sibling r1 files; emits its r2.json). Document the schedule (e.g., 'r1 deadline 2026-05-20T20:00Z; r2 deadline 2026-05-21T20:00Z; synthesis 2026-05-22T12:00Z').

tier2_judgment_findings.title: Audit-chain emission `consensus_debate_complete` is gated on synthesis not yet produced
tier2_judgment_findings.evidence: No audit-chain emission exists. Acceptable — synthesis precedes emission. Flagging to ensure the chain step is not skipped.
tier2_judgment_findings.remediation: After synthesis lands, emit `consensus_debate_complete` with change_id keystone-bundle-2026-05-20 + termination_reason + reviewer_id list + facet count.

tier2_judgment_findings.title: FixupTasks ledger not yet updated with bundle's open gaps
tier2_judgment_findings.doctrine_citation: feedback_multispectrum_review_v22 — 'FixupTasks filed to registries/cross-cutting/fixuptasks.jsonl per CONV-N / TEN-N'
tier2_judgment_findings.evidence: The audit identifies 8 gaps (Gap #1..#8); the deep-dive identifies 25+ F-MISSED-* + 10+ F-ANTI-* + multiple F-PAIN-* findings. None of these have been transcribed to registries/cross-cutting/fixuptasks.jsonl as CONV-N or TEN-N entries. The transcription is a precondition for the lane's bookkeeping.
tier2_judgment_findings.remediation: On synthesis, transcribe each non-blocking finding to fixuptasks.jsonl with a CONV-N or TEN-N identifier and an owner/IP placement.

tier2_judgment_findings.title: Strong positive: bundle authors learned from ADR-0220 → ADR-0239 drift
tier2_judgment_findings.evidence: Every keystone ADR carries the 'partial acceptance rejected because doctrines are mutually-reinforcing' framing, explicitly citing the ADR-0220 → ADR-0239 amendment cycle that occurred within 12 days as the failure mode being prevented. The keystone_position N-of-14 field embeds bundle membership in every ADR's frontmatter. This is exactly the structural discipline the doctrine wants.

tier2_judgment_findings.title: Strong positive: deep-dive's adversarial voice is genuine (not performative)
tier2_judgment_findings.evidence: The deep-dive F-ANTI-1 (Intelligence as the new Universal Gateway) and F-ANTI-7 (substrate dependency depth = distributed monolith) and F-PAIN-1 (hardcoded `oyatie` slug everywhere) are uncomfortable findings that a polite review would suppress. The voice is direct and the migration-pain scoring (1-10) is concrete. This is what bias-collapse-prevention is for: surface the uncomfortable before ratification.

tier2_judgment_findings.title: Strong positive: audit honestly downgrades cross-reference coherence and intern-readability to ORANGE
tier2_judgment_findings.evidence: The audit's §1.4 roll-up explicitly downgrades C2 (bidirectional linkage) to FAIL and C3 (intern-buildability) to PASS-with-issues, with concrete defect counts (~100-200 filenames need normalisation; 6 deliberate placeholders; 1 TBD on roadmap). The honest downgrade is itself evidence the review process is working — a captured audit would have rounded up.

facet_coverage_assessment.explanation: Multispectrum-review v2.4.0 for a CC-1 kernel_public_api change with new microservice boundaries + new HTTP routes + new state machines + breaking-change supersession requires F1-F11 + M1+M2 + F13 (= 13 F+M facets) plus A1..A7 (= 7 adherence facets) for a total of 20 facets. The deep-dive scopes 15 (F1..F9 + M1+M2 + A1..A7). Missing: F10 reversibility, F11 observability, F13 migration. These are not optional — each is independently triggered by a bundle attribute.

trigger_evidence.F10_reversibility_triggered_by: CC-1 kernel public API class + ADR-0245 substrate-vs-product layering (microservice boundary changes) + ADR-0250 build-ahead doctrine (deliberate placeholders introduce reversibility surface)
trigger_evidence.F11_observability_triggered_by: ADR-0253 network topology adds new HTTP/3 routes; deep-dive F-MISSED-9 identifies missing observability emission contract; ADR-0252 state machine changes for HLC/TrueTime

review_process_doctrine_followed_assessm.explanation: Two of the three doctrinal requirements are met: (1) the change has a clearly-articulated review target (multispectrum-review-v2.4.0) — MET; (2) the bundle is staged with explicit `enforcement_status` and `keystone_position` frontmatter — MET. The third requirement is NOT met: per-facet independent subagent dispatch has not yet happened. The deep-dive consolidates 15+ facet lenses into a single document, which structurally violates the consensus-debate-spectrum-lens-subagents directive even though its CONTENT is high-quality.

evidence_synthesis_quality_assessment.explanation: The two input artefacts (audit + deep-dive) are individually high-quality, mutually-referential, honest about their own limits, and concrete. The audit cites specific filename drift examples and counts placeholders by occurrence. The deep-dive scores every finding on severity (P0/P1/P2) and reversibility cost (1-10). Both artefacts are intern-readable per the user's quality bar. The synthesis itself has not yet been produced, but the raw material is sufficient to produce a strong synthesis once the per-facet subagent debate completes. The evidence is being incorporated correctly INTO the input layer; what's missing is the per-facet PROCESSING of that evidence through independent subagent lenses.

verdict_summary: From the M2 meta-review lens, the keystone bundle's substantive content earns a CONDITIONAL-GO, but the multispectrum-review v2.4.0 PROCESS itself needs three remediations before synthesis can land: (1) dispatch per-facet independent subagent wave (F1..F11 + M1 + F13 + A1..A7 = 19 distinct subagent sessions) — the deep-dive is INPUT, not the review; (2) add the missing F10 + F11 + F13 facets to the wave; (3) explicitly declare change_class CC-1 kernel_public_api and trigger evidence per facet. The audit + deep-dive together form a STRONG evidence package; the missing layer is the per-facet independent processing of that evidence.
